Hi Amanda / Elliot —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the concrete next steps we discussed so the whole team has the same picture. I’ve left the technical owners (Ben and Jordan) on cc for sizing and procurement asks.

Key pain & goals (your words):
- Latency-sensitive clinical inference (sub-100ms p95 for short prompts) for triage flows; peak periods tied to morning shift windows.
- Data isolation requirement: customer PII processed in a fully isolated dedicated pool (no multi-tenant sharing).
- Predictable monthly spend for budgeting — you need committed monthly throughput with defined burst behavior.

What we propose (summary):
- Dedicated capacity: a reserved GPU pool with tenant isolation (network & storage boundaries) + a canary pool for safe rollouts.
- SLA targets: 99.9% availability for reserved pool; typical p95 latency target 80–120ms depending on model/sequence length.
- Bursting: configurable burst capacity (up to 25% of baseline) with throttled fallbacks to compatible quantized model variants.

Open items / asks we agreed on:
1) Sizing: Lyra to share 2 weeks of traffic sample (call volume and typical prompt lengths). Ben/Jordan to provide a first-pass sizing matrix once we have that.
2) Compliance: Lyra would like a SOC 2 snapshot and confirmation of KMS/HSM options for key material — attached soc2-snapshot.pdf and redwood-mop-draft.docx.
3) Procurement: target commercial terms (monthly committed GPU hours + burst clause). We shared a rough estimate (attached lyra-prod-estimate.xlsx).
4) Rollout & runbook: operations playbook (we proposed an initial canary + automated fallback plan).

Next steps (owners & ETA):
- Amanda/Elliot: share anonymized traffic sample + procurement contact (ETA: end of week, 08/22).
- Ben Carter: provide sizing worksheet and preliminary throughput buckets (ETA: 08/19).
- Rishi Malhotra: confirm isolation architecture options and typical latency profile per model family (ETA: 08/19).
- Kimberly Park: set up commercial checklist and draft term sheet for review (ETA: 08/20).

If that aligns, I’ll schedule a follow-up on Wednesday (08/20) for a technical walk-through and procurement sync.

Thanks —

Amanda — quick technical addendum ahead of the Wednesday walkthrough. High level notes so procurement/infra have crisp expectations: 

1) Isolation model options (tradeoffs):
   - Full private pool (recommended): physical tenant isolation with dedicated nodes + private networking. Pros: simplest audit trail and easiest to meet strict PIIs. Cons: higher baseline cost.
   - Logical isolation on shared hardware: namespaces + runtime enforcement. Pros: lower cost; Cons: harder for certs/attestation and some customers disallow.

2) Latency expectations:
   - For short prompts (<=32 tokens) on a tuned FP16 / quantized 4-bit variant on A100-class hardware, we typically see p95 in the 60–95ms range when KV cache hit rates are high and batching is constrained to low-latency windows.
   - Under 2x peak concurrency without batching, p95 can degrade to ~120–160ms depending on prompt shape. Canary validation on your actual traffic is the only reliable confirmation.

3) Canary plan (proposal):
   - Week 0: deploy a small private pool (10% estimated capacity) with identical model weights and ops tracing.
   - Week 1: run mirrored traffic (traffic shadowing) during a single peak window, collect p95 and KV cache hit metrics.
   - Gate: require p95 <= 100ms and successful failover runbook execution in 95% of failover trials before increasing commit.

4) SLA routing & fallback:
   - Primary: reserved private pool (SLA 99.9% availability).
   - Secondary (optional): fallback to quantized, compatible model variant in Redwood-hosted shared pool (cost-optimized) during sustained capacity constraints; this preserves availability but may slightly alter output quality.

I’ll bring sample telemetry dashboards and the runbook excerpt to the 08/20 call. Ben — I left the sizing template in the shared Drive link Kimberly included; can you produce the line-item estimate for procurement?

- Rishi
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
